reported.title: SQL injection: search term interpolated into query string
reported.body: `search()` builds its SQL with an f-string: `WHERE owner_id = {user["id"]} AND documents_fts MATCH '{term}'`. `term` arrives unfiltered from `handle_search(token, term, ...)` in `app/__init__.py`. A term containing a single quote terminates the literal and lets the caller append arbitrary SQL (e.g. `x' OR 1=1 --`), which both defeats the `owner_id` restriction (exposing other users' documents) and allows arbitrary statements against the database. `db.query` supports bound parameters (see `db.py:20`), and `suggest()` in the same file does it correctly.

reported.title: purge_user swallows the admin check with bare except
reported.body: `_assert_admin(user)` is wrapped in `try/except Exception: pass`, so the `Forbidden` it raises is discarded and the purge runs for every caller, admin or not. Any authenticated user can delete all documents of an arbitrary `target_user_id`. Additionally the follow-up `DELETE FROM shares WHERE doc_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM documents)` is unscoped and removes orphaned share rows belonging to all users, not just the target.

reported.title: delete_document performs no admin or ownership check
reported.body: `_assert_admin` is defined in this module but never called from `delete_document`, and there is no owner check either — the DELETE is keyed only on the request-supplied `doc_id`. `handle_delete_document` in `app/__init__.py` exposes this to any authenticated session, so any user can delete any other user's document. Compare `documents.get_document`, which verifies `owner_id == user["id"] or user["is_admin"]`.

reported.title: Path traversal: export filename is joined without validation
reported.body: `export_path` joins the caller-supplied `filename` straight into the export directory with no sanitisation. `handle_export(token, doc_id, filename)` passes it through unmodified, so a filename such as `../../../etc/cron.d/job` escapes the user directory, and an absolute path (`/etc/cron.d/job`) is honoured outright by `os.path.join`, discarding the prefix. `export_document` then writes JSON to that location, giving an authenticated user an arbitrary-file-write primitive. The repo already has `validators.safe_export_name` for this, used by `reports.write_report`.

reported.title: SSRF: user-supplied URL fetched with no scheme or host allowlist
reported.body: `fetch_remote_document` performs `requests.get(url)` on a URL supplied directly by the caller via `handle_import_url`, with no scheme validation, no host/IP allowlist, and redirects followed by default. An authenticated user can make the server request internal endpoints such as `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` or services on localhost/private ranges; the response body is returned to the caller in the `body` field, so the data is exfiltrated too.

reported.title: audit.record called with swapped arguments, raising ValueError
reported.body: `audit.record` has signature `record(action, user_id, doc_id, detail="")` (audit.py:6). The call passes the user dict as `action` and the string `"document.report"` as `user_id`, so `int(user_id)` raises `ValueError: invalid literal for int()`. This happens after the report file has already been written, so the caller sees an exception for an operation that partially succeeded, and no audit row is ever recorded for report exports.

reported.title: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded development value
reported.body: `SECRET_KEY` now defaults to the publicly known string "dev-secret-change-me" instead of failing fast when `QUORUM_DEMO_SECRET` is unset. `auth.sign` uses this key to HMAC session tokens (`auth.py:14-15`) and share signatures. A deployment where the env var is missing silently runs with a known key, so anyone can forge a `<user_id>.<signature>` session token for any user, including an admin, and can forge share-link signatures. The removed `os.environ[...]` lookup was the protection against this.

reported.title: Page-size clamp removed, allowing unbounded result sets
reported.body: Removing `min(int(limit), Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE)` means `handle_list_documents(token, limit=10**9)` will pull the entire documents table into memory and materialise it as a list of dicts. This is a trivially reachable resource-exhaustion vector for any authenticated caller, and it leaves `Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE` unused.

reported.title: Mutable default argument for scopes is mutated in place
reported.body: `scopes: list = []` creates a single list object shared by every call that omits the argument, and line 20 appends to it. The default list is permanently mutated to `["read"]` after the first call, and any caller that does pass a list has their list modified in place. Any future code that appends further scopes to the default would leak those scopes into all subsequent share links. Use `scopes: list = None` and build a fresh list inside the function.

reported.title: Scope check for document.report always passes
reported.body: `permissions.has_scope` returns True for any action absent from `REQUIRED_SCOPES` (documented explicitly in permissions.py lines 5-8 and 21-27). `"document.report"` is not a key in that table, so this guard is inert and every caller of `write_report` passes it regardless of their scopes. Either add `"document.report": "documents:write"` to `REQUIRED_SCOPES` or check an action that is already listed.

reported.title: Share links never expire: TTL stored as duration and never checked
reported.body: `expires_at = (ttl or DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS)` stores a relative duration, not an absolute expiry timestamp, into the `expires_in` column. `resolve_share_link` never reads or compares that column at all, so every share link remains valid indefinitely and a leaked link grants permanent access to the document. Store `time.time() + (ttl or DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS)` and reject rows whose expiry has passed in `resolve_share_link`.

reported.title: Share signature compared with == instead of constant-time compare
reported.body: `resolve_share_link` compares the expected HMAC against the caller-supplied `signature` using `!=`, which short-circuits on the first differing byte. This is a timing oracle that lets an attacker recover a valid signature byte by byte for a doc_id/token pair. `auth.verify_session_token` already uses `hmac.compare_digest` for exactly this reason; do the same here (requires importing `hmac`). Note also that the returned document ignores the `scopes` stored on the share row.

reported.title: TOCTOU between existence check and file write, widened by sleep
reported.body: The `os.path.exists(destination)` guard and the subsequent `open(destination, "w")` are separated by a deliberate 0.2s sleep. In that window the path can be created or replaced (for example by a symlink pointing elsewhere), and the `"w"` open follows the symlink and truncates the target. Since the destination directory is under a shared export root, this turns the check into no protection at all. Use `open(destination, "x")` and let `FileExistsError` propagate rather than pre-checking.

reported.title: Formatter registry references modules that do not exist
reported.body: `FORMATTERS` maps every format to `app.formatters.*`, but there is no `formatters` package in `benchmark/seeded-bugs/app/` (the directory contains only the flat modules). Every call to `load_formatter` therefore raises `ModuleNotFoundError`, while `available_formats()` — exported as `handle_available_formats` — advertises all three formats as supported. The registry itself is a safe hardcoded allowlist; the problem is that the targets are missing.

reported.body: `search()` builds the statement with an f-string that interpolates the user-supplied `term` (and `user["id"]`) directly into the SQL, and `db.query` passes it verbatim to `sqlite3.execute`. reported.title: Admin check in purge_user swallowed by bare except
reported.body: `_assert_admin(user)` is wrapped in `try/except Exception: pass`, so the `Forbidden` it raises is discarded and execution continues. A non-admin caller therefore reaches `DELETE FROM documents WHERE owner_id = ?` for any `target_user_id` and can destroy another user's entire document set. An authorization check whose failure is silently ignored is equivalent to no check at all.

reported.title: delete_document performs no ownership or admin check
reported.body: `delete_document` issues `DELETE FROM documents WHERE id = ?` without calling `_assert_admin` and without any ownership check via `documents.get_document`. It is exposed to every authenticated caller through `handle_delete_document` in `app/__init__.py`, so any logged-in user can delete any other user's document simply by supplying its id. Call `get_document(doc_id, user)` first (it raises `Forbidden` for non-owners and non-admins) or `_assert_admin(user)`, depending on the intended policy.

reported.title: Export filename joined without sanitisation allows path traversal
reported.body: `export_path` joins the raw, user-supplied `filename` onto the export directory with no validation. The repository already has `validators.safe_export_name`, which `reports.write_report` uses for exactly this purpose. Via `handle_export(token, doc_id, "../../../tmp/x")` an authenticated user writes attacker-influenced JSON content to an arbitrary path with the service's privileges, overwriting files outside the export root. Sanitise the name with `validators.safe_export_name(filename)` (adding `from . import validators`) before joining, or verify the realpath stays under `user_dir`.

reported.title: SSRF: user-supplied URL fetched with no scheme or host allowlist
reported.body: `fetch_remote_document` is reached from `handle_import_url` with a fully caller-controlled `url` and performs `requests.get` with no scheme validation, no host allowlist, and redirects followed by default. An authenticated user can target `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` or any internal-only service, and the response body is returned to them in the `body` field, exfiltrating cloud credentials or internal data. Restrict the scheme to http/https, resolve the host and reject loopback/link-local/private addresses, disable redirects (or re-validate each hop), and cap the number of bytes read from the response.

reported.title: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded development value
reported.body: `SECRET_KEY` now defaults to the literal `"dev-secret-change-me"`. This value is the HMAC key used by `auth.sign()` for session tokens (`<user_id>.<signature>`) and for share-link signatures. If `QUORUM_DEMO_SECRET` is unset in any deployment, the signing key is publicly known and anyone can forge a session token for an arbitrary user id, completely bypassing authentication. The previous fail-fast `os.environ[...]` lookup was the only thing preventing the service from running with a known key.

reported.title: Page size clamp removed, allowing unbounded result sets
reported.body: Dropping `min(int(limit), Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE)` makes the page size fully caller-controlled. A single `handle_list_documents(token, limit=10**9)` request pulls the entire `documents` table into memory and materialises it as a list of dicts, giving any authenticated user a cheap memory-exhaustion lever. If the export UI needs bigger pages, raise `MAX_PAGE_SIZE` instead of removing the bound.

reported.title: Mutable default argument mutated in create_share_link
reported.body: `scopes: list = []` is a shared mutable default that is then mutated via `scopes.append("read")`. The appended value persists in the default object across calls, and when a caller does pass a list it is mutated in place as a side effect. `handle_create_share` invokes the two-argument form for the default case, hitting this path directly.

reported.title: TOCTOU between existence check and export file write
reported.body: The `os.path.exists(destination)` check is followed by a deliberate 200 ms `time.sleep` and then `open(destination, "w")`. Two concurrent exports of the same filename both pass the existence check, and the second write silently truncates the first file. An atomic exclusive create closes the window.

reported.title: has_scope check for document.report always passes
reported.body: `permissions.has_scope(user, "document.report")` is a no-op guard: `document.report` is absent from `permissions.REQUIRED_SCOPES`, and that module's `has_scope` returns `True` for any unlisted action (stated explicitly in its docstring and module header). Every caller therefore passes this check regardless of the scopes they hold, so report export is effectively unprotected. Add `"document.report"` to `REQUIRED_SCOPES` with the appropriate required scope before relying on this check.

reported.title: audit.record called with arguments in the wrong order
reported.body: `audit.record` has the signature `record(action, user_id, doc_id, detail="")` and does `int(user_id)`. Here a user dict is passed as `action` and the string `"document.report"` as `user_id`, so `int("document.report")` raises `ValueError`. The report file has already been written by that point, so `write_report` always fails after its side effects and no audit row is ever written for report exports.

reported.title: Share links never expire; TTL stored but never enforced
reported.body: `expires_at` is only the TTL in seconds (a duration, not an absolute timestamp) written into the `expires_in` column, and `resolve_share_link` selects just `doc_id, scopes` and never compares anything against the current time. Any share token therefore grants access to the document indefinitely, defeating the documented TTL. Store an absolute expiry (`time.time() + ttl`) and reject expired rows in `resolve_share_link`. Note also that `ttl or DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS` converts an explicit `ttl=0` into the full 7-day default.

reported.title: Share signature compared with non-constant-time !=
reported.body: The HMAC signature check uses `expected != signature`, which short-circuits at the first differing byte and is timing-variable, unlike `auth.verify_session_token` which correctly uses `hmac.compare_digest` for the same purpose. Import `hmac` and use `if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature):` here as well.

Any authenticated user can destroy any other user's documents, and the log line attributes the deletion to them. Add an ownership/admin check (e.g. `get_document(doc_id, user)` first, or `WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ?` for non-admins) plus the `document.delete` scope check that `permissions.REQUIRED_SCOPES` already defines.

reported.title: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded development value
reported.body: `SECRET_KEY` now defaults to the literal `"dev-secret-change-me"` when `QUORUM_DEMO_SECRET` is unset, replacing the fail-fast `os.environ[...]` lookup. `auth.sign()` uses this key for session tokens (`verify_session_token` accepts `<user_id>.<hmac(user_id)>`) and `sharing` uses it for share signatures. Any deployment started without the environment variable now boots silently and signs with a value published in this repository, so anyone can forge a session token for an arbitrary user id — including an admin — with no credentials.

reported.title: list_documents no longer clamps limit to MAX_PAGE_SIZE
reported.body: The `min(int(limit), Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE)` clamp was removed, so `handle_list_documents(token, limit=10**9)` passes the caller's value straight into `LIMIT` and the whole result set is materialised into a list of dicts in memory. Any authenticated user can force the process to read and buffer the entire documents table for their owner id — a cheap memory-exhaustion / DoS lever. `Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE` is now unused.

reported.title: export_path joins an unsanitised filename, allowing writes outside export root
reported.body: `export_path()` does `os.path.join(user_dir, filename)` with the raw caller-supplied `filename` from `handle_export(token, doc_id, filename)`. A value like `../../../../etc/cron.d/pwn`, or an absolute path (os.path.join discards the prefix when the second argument is absolute), escapes the per-user export directory, and `export_document` then opens it with mode "w", overwriting arbitrary files with attacker-influenced JSON under the service account. The repo already has `validators.safe_export_name()` for this (used by `reports.write_report`); apply it before joining, or verify the realpath stays under `user_dir` as `indexer.extract_text` does.

reported.title: SSRF: server-side GET to an arbitrary user-supplied URL
reported.body: `fetch_remote_document()` passes `url`, supplied directly by the caller via `handle_import_url`, to `requests.get` with no scheme or host validation and with redirects enabled by default. A caller can target `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/`, localhost admin ports, or any internal host reachable from the server, and the response body is handed back to them in the `body` field. Validate the scheme (http/https only), resolve and allowlist the host, and either disable redirects or re-validate each hop.

reported.title: SQL injection: search term interpolated into query via f-string
reported.body: `search()` builds its SQL with an f-string and splices `user["id"]` and the caller-supplied `term` directly into the statement: `WHERE owner_id = {user["id"]} AND documents_fts MATCH '{term}'`. `term` arrives unescaped from `handle_search(token, term, ...)`. A term containing a single quote terminates the literal and lets the caller append arbitrary SQL (e.g. `x' OR 1=1 --`), dropping the owner_id restriction and returning other users' documents; a UNION SELECT reaches any table. Every other query in the codebase uses bound parameters (`suggest()` right below does). `column` is safe because it comes from the SORTABLE allowlist, so only the values need parameterising.

reported.title: Share signature compared with != instead of constant-time compare
reported.body: `resolve_share_link` compares the recomputed HMAC against the caller-supplied `signature` with `expected != signature`. Python string comparison short-circuits at the first differing byte, leaking how much of the signature is correct through timing and enabling byte-by-byte recovery of a valid signature for a chosen doc_id/token. `auth.verify_session_token` already uses `hmac.compare_digest` for precisely this reason; do the same here (add `import hmac`, then `if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature or "")`).

reported.title: audit.record called with arguments in the wrong order
reported.body: `audit.record` is declared `record(action: str, user_id: int, doc_id: int, detail: str = "")` and coerces the second and third arguments with `int()`. The call here is `audit.record(user, "document.report", doc_id)`, so `action` receives the user dict and `user_id` receives the string `"document.report"`; `int("document.report")` raises ValueError. The report file has already been written at that point, so every `write_report` call fails after producing the file and no audit row is ever written.

reported.title: write_report scope check is a no-op: action absent from REQUIRED_SCOPES
reported.body: `permissions.has_scope` returns True for any action absent from `REQUIRED_SCOPES` (its module docstring warns: "a privileged action missing from this table is not merely unprotected — the check silently passes"). `REQUIRED_SCOPES` lists only `document.read`, `document.share`, `document.delete`, `document.export` — not `document.report`. So `if not permissions.has_scope(user, "document.report")` is never true and the `Forbidden` is unreachable; any authenticated user can write reports regardless of scopes. Add `"document.report": "documents:write"` to `permissions.REQUIRED_SCOPES`.

reported.title: Share links never expire; TTL stored as a duration and never checked
reported.body: `expires_at = (ttl or DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS)` stores a duration (e.g. 604800), not an absolute timestamp, in the `expires_in` column, and `resolve_share_link` selects only `doc_id, scopes` and never compares anything against the current time. Every minted share link therefore stays valid forever and the `ttl` argument has no effect. Store an absolute expiry (`time.time() + (ttl or DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS)`) and reject expired rows on resolve. `resolve_share_link` also ignores the stored `scopes` and returns the entire document row regardless of what the link was scoped to.

reported.title: Mutable default argument for scopes is shared and mutated across calls
reported.body: `scopes: list = []` is evaluated once at definition time and `scopes.append("read")` mutates that shared object, so the default list is permanently modified after the first call. When a caller does pass a list (as `handle_create_share` does), it is mutated in place and the caller's object silently gains a scope. Use `scopes: list = None` and build a fresh list inside the function (`scopes = list(scopes or [])`).

reported.title: export_document skips the document.export scope check
reported.body: `permissions.REQUIRED_SCOPES` declares `"document.export": "documents:write"`, and the sibling `reports.write_report` performs a `has_scope` check before writing. `export_document` performs none: `handle_export` only authenticates, `get_document` only enforces ownership, and the file is written regardless of whether the session holds `documents:write`. A read-only session can therefore perform a write-scoped action.

reported.title: Unbounded read of the remote response body
reported.body: `response.text` materialises the whole remote body in memory with no size cap. Because the URL is caller-controlled, pointing the importer at a very large or endless response (the 10s timeout applies per socket operation, not to total transfer) lets a single request exhaust process memory. Stream the response and abort past a maximum byte count.

reported.title: TOCTOU between existence check and truncating write in export_document
reported.body: `os.path.exists(destination)` is followed by a deliberate `time.sleep(0.2)` and then `open(destination, "w")`, which truncates. Anything created at that path during the 200 ms window — including a concurrent export of the same filename, or a symlink planted by another process with access to the export root — is silently overwritten, so the `FileExistsError` guard does not actually hold. Open with mode `"x"` and let the exclusive create fail instead of pre-checking.

reported.title: FORMATTERS registry points at modules that do not exist
reported.body: Every entry maps to `app.formatters.*`, but there is no `formatters` package under `benchmark/seeded-bugs/app/` (the package contains only admin, audit, auth, config, db, documents, export, fetcher, indexer, permissions, plugins, reports, search, sharing, validators). `load_formatter("markdown")` therefore raises ModuleNotFoundError for every registered name, and `available_formats()` — exposed without authentication via `handle_available_formats()` — advertises three formats none of which can be loaded.

survived.title: purge_user swallows the admin check with a bare except
survived.body: The admin gate is wrapped in `try: _assert_admin(user) / except Exception: pass`. `_assert_admin` signals failure by raising `Forbidden`, so the exception is caught and discarded and execution falls through to the deletes. The check therefore always passes: any authenticated non-admin can call `purge_user` and delete every document owned by an arbitrary `target_user_id`, plus share rows. A failing authorization check must propagate.
